aggregation_note: Never average rates. Sum the levels (persons_thousands) over regions, sexes or months, then divide. SCB's own annual and county figures are published; prefer them over recomputing.
Sum levels then divide; prefer published annual and county figures.
Sum levels then divide.
Seasonally adjusted monthly series: for annual values use the unadjusted series; a mean of adjusted months is not an official figure.
As above.
Population on 31 December: add regions, never add years. Years under the cell key method carry small per-cell noise.
Rolling twelve months: December is the calendar year, and months must not be averaged or added. Across regions, ages or sexes, sum sick_pay_days and insured_persons, then divide.
Started cases are a flow: add months and regions. Suppressed counts are NULL; a sum over them is a lower bound.
Flow; F00-F99. National only.
Flow; F43 by county. Inside F00-F99; never add to it.
A stock at month end: add regions and ages, never months. For a year, average the months or take December.
Kolada publishes county and national values; use them. A population-weighted mean of municipalities approximates them (the denominator is ages 18-65).
Prefer published county and national values.
Sick-pay days per insured, annual. Prefer published county and national values; the insured population is the right weight and is not in Kolada.
Ill-health days per insured. Prefer published values.
A median cannot be aggregated from medians: use Kolada's county and national values, never a mean of municipal medians.
Prefer published values.
Survey estimate (Folkhälsomyndigheten) republished per municipality; small municipalities have wide intervals, and a weighted mean does not narrow them.

Reported crime is counted where it happened, not where people live: a population-weighted mean of municipalities misses the published county value by 15% on average (up to 86%). Use Kolada's county and national values.
Share of year-9 pupils; the pupil count is not in the model. Use published county and national values.
